blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Condo buildings in Sumas Mountain
Streets, schools and getting around Sumas Mountain

items.t: Sumas Mountain rises between Abbotsford and Chilliwack, above Sumas Prairie to the south and the Fraser River lowland to the north. The built part is inside the City of Abbotsford; the upper and eastern rural part is unincorporated Fraser Valley Regional District (FVRD) land.
City-side neighbourhoods on the west and south slopes include Auguston, McKee and the Eagle Mountain side; Clayburn Village sits at the northwest foot.

Main roads are Sumas Mountain Road (becoming Upper Sumas Mountain Road toward the regional park), McKee Road, Dawson Road and Whatcom Road, connecting down to Highway 1 at the Whatcom Road interchange at the south foot.

Schools on the slopes: Auguston Traditional Elementary, 36367 Stephen Leacock Drive; Mountain Elementary, 2299 Mountain Drive; Irene Kelleher Totí:ltawtxw Elementary, 2540 Eagle Mountain Drive. No secondary school is on the mountain.
Transit: BC Transit routes 7 (Sumas Mountain), 9 (McKee) and 15 (Auguston) serve the built slopes and the foot.

Where condo stock actually concentrates: nowhere on the mountain. There is no tower, no low-rise apartment corridor and no town centre on the slopes — the housing is detached houses in the City neighbourhoods and rural homes on large lots above. SnapStats recorded attached (condos & townhomes) inventory of 0 and sales of 0 for Sumas Mountain in September 2026.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Sumas Mountain

items.t: Form B (Strata Property Act, s.59): — the disclosure certificate for any strata lot (including a bare-land strata lot at Straiton or a townhouse at Junction Creek): monthly fee, approved levies, CRF balance, parking/storage, proceedings, plus an insurance summary required since April 1, 2023.

Rental bylaws void: since November 24, 2022 (long-term); short-term rentals may still be restricted. Directory lines such as "rentals allowed w/restrictions" for Junction Creek do not restore a long-term rental ban.
55+ bylaws (ss.123.1/123.2): — the only permitted age bylaw is 55+, with the May 1, 2023 expanded exemptions.

Two governments, two rule books: City side: Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw 2400 (2014) — Country Residential minimum lot 2.0 ha, Suburban Residential 0.4 ha, Rural Residential 4.0 ha — and Abbotsforward 2050, OCP Bylaw 2600-2016, with the McKee Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 3400-2023) as OCP Schedule E for the west slope. Rural side: the FVRD Sumas Mountain Official Community Plan, Consolidated OCP Bylaw No. 584, with no public sewer or water at rural density (wells and septic).

Steep-slope control: The City OCP includes a Steep Slope Development Permit Area, and the McKee plan protects unstable geotechnical areas and slopes over 40% as open space — the practical reason future multi-family form here is planned as ground-oriented product at the foot, not apartment buildings on the slopes.

PTT: 1% / 2% / 3% general structure (+2% over $3M residential); first-time buyer exemption on the first $500,000 (max $8,000) up to $835,000, partial to $860,000; Newly Built Home Exemption full to $1,100,000, out at $1,150,000.
HBP $60,000 / FHSA $8,000 per year, $40,000 lifetime
CMHC premiums 0.6%–4.5%: of the mortgage amount; insurance required under 20% down on homes $1.5M or less.

Tax split on the mountain: City-side taxes were due July 2, 2026 (5% penalty July 3, second 5% September 16, 2026). Rural FVRD-side property is taxed by the Province (Surveyor of Taxes), due July 2 under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act, s.11, with 5% after July 2 and a further 5% after October 31.

blocks.text: Good to know about Sumas Mountain

items.t: The next housing on the mountain is planned at its foot, in ground-oriented form. It is a proposal at the foot of the mountain — not a presale, and not condos.

The McKee Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 3400-2023) is Schedule E of the City OCP and guides the west-slope mountainside neighbourhood; its Urban 2 – Ground Oriented designation is where townhome/multiplex forms are planned.

A new McKee neighbourhood park is in planning near Dawson Road and Sumas Mountain Road, and a McKee Trail Strategy is being built for the trail network — both signal where City investment is going on the slopes: parks and ground-oriented neighbourhoods, not condo sites.

Lightning Rock was returned to Semá:th (Sumas) First Nation. Semá:th states ownership of the culturally significant Lightning Rock site on the mountain was transferred to the Nation under an agreement with the Province, and that an alternate quarry-truck route study was agreed by the Province, Semá:th and the City — context any buyer on the quarry routes should know.

Chilliwack got an SSMUH extension next door, Abbotsford did not need the same one for this area: the Province's September 16, 2024 bulletin lists Chilliwack among communities granted a partial extension (Proper neighbourhood / Hazel Park, to December 31, 2030) — relevant if a buyer is comparing the Chilliwack side of the mountain.

blocks.text: Good to know about Sumas Mountain

items.t: The next townhouses on the mountain are planned at its foot, in one proposal. It is a proposal — not built, not a presale, and not counted in.

Two tax systems share one mountain. City-side lots pay City of Abbotsford taxes (due July 2, 2026; 5% penalty July 3 and a second 5% September 16, 2026), while rural FVRD lots pay the Province through the Surveyor of Taxes (due July 2; 5% after July 2 and a further 5% after October 31) — the penalty calendar for a rural cross-shop differs from the City one a townhouse buyer will actually face.

Quarry traffic is part of life on the main road: five quarries operate on Sumas Mountain and their gravel trucks use an access road to Highway 1 through the Lightning Rock site, per Semá:th First Nation, which also states the culturally significant Lightning Rock site was transferred to the Nation under an agreement with the Province. A buyer at Junction Creek or Straiton, both on the Sumas Mountain Road corridor, should drive the route at truck hours before writing.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Sumas Mountain
Bare-land strata

items.t: Straiton / Straiton Mountain Estates — 4595 Sumas Mountain Road. Bare-land strata (Strata Plan EPS1299): A City council report describes the Straiton strata subdivision at this address (owner Straiton Development Corporation) as 26 single-family strata lots on the west side of Sumas Mountain Road, south of Dawson Road — a bare-land-style strata of detached houses, not a townhome or condo building. A listing describing the wider community as a "gated 42 lot" community conflicts with the City report's 26 strata lots.

blocks.text: Fee-simple land

items.t: City slope lots (Auguston, McKee, Eagle Mountain side): single detached homes in built City neighbourhoods on the west and southwest slopes — fee-simple lots in the ordinary form. Lot character follows the City rural/suburban zones where they apply: Country Residential (CR) minimum lot 2.0 ha, Suburban Residential (SR) minimum lot 0.4 ha, Rural Residential (RR) minimum lot 4.0 ha under Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014. These are zone minimums for the zones named, not a claim that every slope lot is that size.

FVRD rural parcels (upper/eastern mountain): rural/country-residential homes on larger lots under the FVRD Sumas Mountain OCP (Bylaw No. 584). The rural part has no public sewer or water at rural density — homes use wells and onsite (septic) services.
City-side servicing contrast: the built City neighbourhoods are the serviced side of the mountain; the servicing statement documented is the FVRD side's well/septic position above.

ALR: the OCP includes an ALR map (Map 16) and shows an Agriculture designation on the east side of the mountain; whether any single parcel is in the ALR must be checked parcel by parcel — no ALR percentage split is stated.

Slope/open-space character: the McKee plan area's open space network is made up of streamside setbacks, critical habitat, geotechnical areas and slopes over 40%, with trail corridors in the McKee Trail Strategy — a material share of mountainside "land" is protected open space, not buildable lot area. Price buildable area, not gross area.

Market thinness, labelled correctly: SnapStats recorded Sumas Mountain detached inventory 3 / sales 0 and attached inventory 0 / sales 0 in September 2026. SnapStats has no land category (Detached vs "Condos & Townhomes" combined; Abbotsford community detached median $949,000) — no detached figure is presented as a land figure.

blocks.text: Development proposal

items.t: The City's July 10, 2025 council-consideration notice describes a proposal for the McKee Road lands at the mountain's foot (35922, 35944, 35970, 36070, 36138, 36160 and Lot 17 McKee Road, in the McKee plan area) — approximately 108 single detached lots, 192 townhouses and four rural residential lots, with approximately 5 ha of P2 land for open space and parks.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Sumas Mountain

items.t: "Sumas Mountain" is the FVREB sub-area name in the SnapStats FVR September 2026 report, and the City uses it for the mountainside neighbourhoods on the west and south slopes, including the McKee plan area; the FVRD plan for the rural part is the Sumas Mountain Official Community Plan, Consolidated OCP Bylaw No. 584.

Neighbourhoods inside or at the foot: Auguston, McKee and the Eagle Mountain side on the City slopes; Clayburn Village at the northwest foot. Nearby areas: Abbotsford East (west/southwest foot), Sumas Prairie (south), Chilliwack (east side).

Schools on the slopes: Auguston Traditional Elementary (36367 Stephen Leacock Drive), Mountain Elementary (2299 Mountain Drive), Irene Kelleher Totí:ltawtxw Elementary (2540 Eagle Mountain Drive); Clayburn Middle (35139 Laburnum Avenue) at the northwest foot; no secondary school is on the mountain. Settled SD34 locator runs (documented) SPLIT: 36367 Stephen Leacock Drive → Auguston Traditional Elementary → Clayburn Middle → Robert Bateman Secondary; 2540 Eagle Mountain Drive → Irene Kelleher Totí:ltawtxw Elementary → William A. Fraser Middle → Yale Secondary. There is no single Sumas Mountain catchment — run the exact address.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Sumas Mountain

items.t: Two governments, two rule sets — confirm which governs the lot first: City side: Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014 (CR 2.0 ha / SR 0.4 ha / RR 4.0 ha minimums above) and Abbotsforward 2050 OCP (CURRENT, adopted December 2025; stale "2600-2016"/"2500-2016" citations flagged). Rural side: FVRD Sumas Mountain OCP, Bylaw No. 584. The McKee Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 3400-2023) is Schedule E of the City OCP and guides the west-slope mountainside neighbourhood.

Steep-slope / geotechnical diligence: the City OCP includes a Steep Slope Development Permit Area for slope land, and the McKee plan protects unstable geotechnical areas and slopes over 40% as open space. Budget for geotechnical review on slope lots before subjects come off.

Bare-land strata rules (Straiton — the BC strata block applies in full to the lot): Form B diligence (fees, amounts owed, levies, CRF balance, insurance summary; provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024 (Straiton at 26 lots is inside the requirement); minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions (younger spouse/partner, caregivers, legacy residents, defined children).

ALR rules (east-side/Agriculture-designated ground where ALR applies): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval as the ALC states it; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)) — note the contrast: Straiton is a lawful bare-land strata because its ground is City mountainside strata ground as documented, not an ALR-residence stratification. ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error.

Flood position: the mountain itself is above the floodplain; the floodplain land is at its foot in Sumas Prairie. Slope lots trade flood risk for geotechnical risk — diligence follows the slope rules above, not floodplain setbacks.

Taxes — TWO regimes on one mountain: City part — Abbotsford taxes due July 2, 2026, 5% penalty July 3, 2026, second 5% September 16, 2026. FVRD/rural part — the owner receives the notice from the Province's Surveyor of Taxes and pays the Province, not the FVRD; under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act s.11, rural taxes are due July 2, with 5% added to any portion unpaid on July 2 and a further 5% on any portion unpaid October 31. Do not quote City dates for an FVRD parcel.

Quarry diligence: five quarries operate on Sumas Mountain and gravel trucks use an access road to Highway 1 through the Lightning Rock site (Semá:th First Nation statement); a City report covers extraction to the 170 m elevation at Jamieson Quarry for Mainland Sand & Gravel Ltd. Truck traffic on mountain roads is a lot-level diligence question.

blocks.text: Good to know about Sumas Mountain

items.t: Semá:th First Nation states the Lightning Rock site on the mountain is a culturally significant area in Semá:th traditional territory, and ownership was transferred to Semá:th First Nation under an agreement with the Province — land diligence on the mountain should be alive to that history, and the quarry alternate-route study was agreed by the Province, Semá:th First Nation and the City.

Sumas Mountain Regional Park (39100 Sumas Mountain Forest Service Road, FVRD) — Chadsey Lake Trail, hiking/trail running/mountain biking, hours 7 a.m. to sunset — plus City parks Lower Sumas Mountain Park, McKinley Park, Glenridge Park and Eagle Mountain Park anchor the slopes' open-space network that shapes what land can ever be built on.

No recreation centre, library, shopping centre or grocery store is on the mountain itself — the nearest City recreation centre named is Abbotsford Recreation Centre, 2499 McMillan Road, at the west foot. Mountain land is bought for slope, view and trail access, at the price of a drive for everything else.
A zero-sales month is normal here, not a signal.

blocks.text: Acreage and rural land in Sumas Mountain
The ground in Sumas Mountain

items.t: The two housing worlds that make the acreage: single detached homes in the built City neighbourhoods on the west and southwest slopes (Auguston, McKee, Eagle Mountain side), and rural/country-residential homes on larger lots on the upper and FVRD part of the mountain. Most mountain homes are freehold; bare land strata homes exist in the City part under City zoning (Straiton, above, is the named example).
Serviced vs unserviced ground: the rural (FVRD) part has no public sewer or water at rural density and homes use wells and onsite (septic) services; the built City slopes are the serviced form.

Slope and flood position: the mountain itself is above the floodplain; the floodplain land is at its foot in Sumas Prairie, the low-lying area south of the mountain named in City flood notices and evacuation alerts. On slope lots the constraint is geotechnical, not flood: the McKee plan puts unstable geotechnical areas and slopes over 40% into a protected open space network, and the OCP applies Steep Slope Development Permit guidelines on slope land.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Sumas Mountain

items.t: Two jurisdictions on one mountain: the built part of Sumas Mountain is inside the City of Abbotsford; the upper and eastern rural part is unincorporated Fraser Valley Regional District (FVRD) land, next to the City of Abbotsford / City of Chilliwack boundary. The mountain rises between Abbotsford and Chilliwack, above Sumas Prairie to the south and the Fraser River lowland to the north.

Names: "Sumas Mountain" is the FVREB sub-area name in board data; the City uses "Sumas Mountain" for the mountainside neighbourhoods on the west and south slopes, including the McKee plan area; the FVRD's plan for the rural part is the Sumas Mountain Official Community Plan, Consolidated OCP Bylaw No. 584.

Main roads: Sumas Mountain Road (becoming Upper Sumas Mountain Road toward the regional park), McKee Road, Dawson Road and Whatcom Road, connecting down to Highway 1 at the Whatcom Road interchange at the south foot; Highway 11 north to Mission and the Huntingdon/Sumas border crossing to the south through Sumas Prairie are the city's other links.

Schools on the slopes (Ministry-listed names and addresses): Auguston Traditional Elementary, 36367 Stephen Leacock Dr; Mountain Elementary, 2299 Mountain Dr; Irene Kelleher Totí:ltawtxw Elementary, 2540 Eagle Mountain Drive; Sandy Hill Elementary, 3836 Old Clayburn Rd. Clayburn Middle School, 35139 Laburnum Ave, sits at the northwest foot; no secondary school is on the mountain itself — Robert Bateman Secondary (35045 Exbury Ave) and Yale Secondary (34620 Old Yale Rd) are the east-side secondary schools at the foot, with William A. Fraser Middle School at 34695 Blatchford Way.

Parks and hazards frame: Sumas Mountain Regional Park (FVRD), 39100 Sumas Mountain Forest Service Road, trails linking to a larger network, the Chadsey Lake Trail from the upper parking lot, hiking / trail running / mountain biking listed, hours 7 a.m. to sunset. City parks on the slopes include Lower Sumas Mountain Park, McKinley Park, Glenridge Park and Eagle Mountain Park. The McKee plan area's open space network is streamside setbacks, critical habitat, geotechnical areas and slopes over 40%, with trail corridors in the McKee Trail Strategy; the City OCP includes a Steep Slope Development Permit Area. No recreation centre or library branch is on the mountain; Abbotsford Recreation Centre, 2499 McMillan Road, is at the west foot. The nearest hospital is Abbotsford Regional Hospital and Cancer Centre, 32900 Marshall Rd.

Transit: BC Transit Central Fraser Valley route 7 (Sumas Mountain) runs downtown Abbotsford to Sumas Mountain, route 9 (McKee) runs to McKee, and route 15 (Auguston) serves Auguston at the southwest foot.

items.t: City plan: Abbotsforward 2050 (adopted Dec 2025) CURRENT: The McKee Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 3400-2023) is Schedule E of the City OCP and guides the mountainside neighbourhood on the west slope.

blocks.text: Good to know about Sumas Mountain

items.t: The same mountain has two second-penalty dates: A City-side owner who misses July 2 takes the second 5% on September 16; a rural-side owner takes it on October 31. Neighbours a road apart can be on different tax calendars, different plans and different servicing — the jurisdiction line is the first fact on any mountain parcel.

blocks.text: Mobile and manufactured homes in Sumas Mountain
The park-form stock that does exist here is one bare-land strata of detached houses — owned-land stock in strata form, not a pad park.
The parks and communities

items.t: Homes on own fee-simple lots: the rest of the mountain is single detached homes in the built City neighbourhoods (Auguston, McKee, Eagle Mountain side) and rural/country-residential homes on larger lots on the upper and FVRD part (City zone minimums: Suburban Residential 0.4 ha, Country Residential 2.0 ha, Rural Residential 4.0 ha). A manufactured home on a buyer's own fee-simple lot here would be dealt with through the land title system, not a pad tenancy.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Sumas Mountain

items.t: Neighbourhoods inside or at the foot of the sub-area: Auguston, McKee and the Eagle Mountain side on the City slopes; Clayburn Village sits at the northwest foot. Nearby areas: Abbotsford East (west and southwest foot), Sumas Prairie (south, below the mountain), and Chilliwack on the east side. Main roads are Sumas Mountain Road (becoming Upper Sumas Mountain Road toward the regional park), McKee Road, Dawson Road and Whatcom Road, connecting down to Highway 1 at the Whatcom Road interchange at the south foot.
Fraser Middle → Yale Secondary.

Hazards and servicing shape the ground: the City OCP includes a Steep Slope Development Permit Area, the McKee plan protects unstable geotechnical areas and slopes over 40% as open space, the mountain itself is above the floodplain (the floodplain land is at its foot in Sumas Prairie), and the FVRD rural part has no public sewer or water at rural density — homes there use wells and onsite (septic) services. Five quarries operate on the mountain, with gravel trucks using an access road to Highway 1 through the Lightning Rock site.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect park-home buyers in Sumas Mountain

items.t: City / regional frame: Suites on City ground: one secondary suite in all single detached dwellings under s.140.3.8 (City-report criteria include a 400 m² minimum lot and 12.0 m frontage); Abbotsford's suite cap is UNDER 50% of the principal dwelling, and a coach/garden suite is capped at 15% of lot area to a maximum of 100 m² — Abbotsford's rules only. SSMUH does not apply to pad tenancies.

ALR position (east-side ground, parcel-by-parcel): the OCP includes an ALR map (Map 16) and shows an Agriculture designation on the east side of the mountain. Where ALR applies, the full block governs: subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)) — Straiton is a lawful bare-land strata because its ground is City mountainside strata ground as documented, not an ALR-residence stratification; ALC residence caps are principal 500 m² or less, suite within the principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha); farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by October 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error.

Well / septic / slope diligence (rural and slope lots): check the well record in the provincial GWELLS database and confirm the onsite sewage system was filed under the Sewerage System Regulation by an Authorized Person through Fraser Health; on slope lots, budget for geotechnical review under the Steep Slope Development Permit Area.

blocks.text: Good to know about Sumas Mountain

items.t: "On Sumas Mountain" can mean two governments, two plans and two tax bills: The built slopes are City of Abbotsford (Abbotsforward 2050, Zoning 2400, City taxes); the upper and eastern rural part is FVRD land (Sumas Mountain OCP Bylaw 584, no public water/sewer, provincial rural taxes due July 2 with penalties July 2 and October 31).

The quarries are part of the mountain's daily life: Five quarries operate on Sumas Mountain and their gravel trucks use an access road to Highway 1 through the Lightning Rock site — a culturally significant area in Semá:th (Sumas) First Nation traditional territory whose ownership was transferred to Semá:th First Nation under an agreement with the Province. Ask about quarry truck traffic on the mountain roads before subjects, not after.

The care and 55+ stock is down the mountain, not on it: Every known 55+ ownership complex in Abbotsford sits in Abbotsford West / Central Abbotsford, with a small cluster on the Abbotsford East side — a downsizer set on the mountain itself has Straiton (not age-restricted) and fee-simple houses, and nothing else on the record.

blocks.text: Duplexes and half duplexes in Sumas Mountain
What a duplex looks like in Sumas Mountain

items.t: The usual duplex form: City zoning minimum lots run from 0.4 ha in the Suburban Residential (SR) zone to 2.0 ha (Country Residential, CR) and 4.0 ha (Rural Residential, RR) under Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014. Most mountain homes are freehold; the rural FVRD part has no public sewer or water at rural density and homes use wells and onsite (septic) services.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect duplexes in Sumas Mountain

items.t: On the rural side, the FVRD Sumas Mountain Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 584) covers the unincorporated part, and the two rule sets differ.

Zoning, SSMUH and suites (Abbotsford): The Abbotsford suite rule is its own: A secondary suite is capped at under 50% of the principal dwelling's habitable area, and a coach/garden suite is limited to 15% of the lot to a maximum of 100 m² — that 15%/100 m² rule is Abbotsford only and is never borrowed for another city.

Slope, flood and ALR: The McKee plan puts unstable geotechnical areas and slopes over 40% into a protected open space network — budget for geotechnical review on slope lots. The mountain itself is above the floodplain; the floodplain land is at its foot in Sumas Prairie. The OCP's Agricultural Land Reserve map (Map 16) shows an Agriculture designation on the east side of the mountain.

Wells and septic (rural lots): The rural part has no public water or sewer — check the well record in the Province's gwells application and confirm the septic system was installed by an Authorized Person under the Sewerage System Regulation through Fraser Health.

faq.a: The strata choices that exist are detached-house bare-land strata (Straiton) and a townhouse complex at the foot (Junction Creek).
faq.q: Is there any condo tower or low-rise I can buy on Sumas Mountain?

faq.a: You own your detached house and lot as a strata lot and share common property (roads, gate, landscaping) with the strata corporation — the City report records 26 single-family strata lots in EPS1299 at 4595 Sumas Mountain Road. Fees, bylaws and a Form B apply exactly as in a condo, but there is no shared building envelope.
faq.q: What is a bare-land strata, and how is Straiton different from a condo?

faq.a: The building directory records "pets allowed, pets allowed w/rest." for the complex — confirm the exact number/size rules in the filed bylaws attached to the Form B, because directory summaries conflict between its own pages.
faq.q: Are pets allowed at Junction Creek?

faq.a: Long-term rental-restriction bylaws are void province-wide since November 24, 2022; a strata may still restrict short-term rentals.
faq.q: Can I rent out a strata home on the mountain?

faq.a: Only what that strata's budget covers — typically common roads, gates, landscaping and insurance on common property, not your house's roof or exterior.
faq.q: What will strata fees cover in a bare-land strata?

faq.a: There are three townhouse strata complexes: Junction Creek (Lower Sumas Mountain Road), Sage at Auguston (4401 Blauson Blvd, 120 units) and King's Gate (36260 McKee Road, 67 units). Everything else named on the mountain is detached houses, rural lots, or the Straiton bare-land strata.
faq.q: Are there actually townhouses on Sumas Mountain, or is it all houses?

faq.a: You own your detached house and lot as a strata lot and share common property (roads, gate, landscaping) with the strata corporation — the City report records 26 single-family strata lots in EPS1299 at 4595 Sumas Mountain Road. Fees, bylaws and a Form B apply exactly as in a townhouse strata, but there is no shared building envelope and no townhouse unit.
faq.q: What is a bare-land strata, and how is Straiton different from a townhouse?

faq.a: King's Gate's complex data expressly records "Age Restrictions: No," and no age restriction appears for Sage at Auguston (a family community beside Auguston Traditional Elementary) or Junction Creek. Gated is not 55+.
faq.q: Are any of the mountain townhouse complexes 55+?

faq.a: Acreage here is individual City slope parcels (zone minimums 0.4 ha SR to 4.0 ha RR) and FVRD rural parcels on well and septic.
faq.q: Is there an acreage subdivision on Sumas Mountain I can buy into?

faq.a: The built west/south slopes are City of Abbotsford (Zoning 2400-2014, Abbotsforward 2050, McKee Plan on the west slope; taxes due July 2 with 5% July 3 and a second 5% September 16). The upper/eastern rural part is FVRD land (Sumas Mountain OCP Bylaw No. 584; provincial rural taxes, second 5% penalty October 31, no public water or sewer). Confirm the lot's side of the line before relying on any rule.
faq.q: Which government governs my lot — and why does it change the taxes?

faq.a: Geotechnical review: the McKee plan puts unstable geotechnical areas and slopes over 40% into a protected open space network, and the OCP applies Steep Slope Development Permit guidelines on slope land — budget for the review and read the lot's DPA position before valuing buildable area.
faq.q: What diligence does a slope acreage need that a flat lot does not?

faq.a: Ask about it directly: five quarries operate on Sumas Mountain and their gravel trucks use an access road to Highway 1 through the Lightning Rock site, per Semá:th First Nation, with an alternate-route study agreed by the Province, Semá:th and the City. A Sumas Mountain Road acreage lives with that traffic until any reroute exists.
faq.q: What about quarry traffic?

faq.a: None that I know of. Abbotsford's known pad-rental parks are Paradise Park, Georgian Park and Maplewood Estates, on other grounds.
faq.q: Is there a mobile home park on Sumas Mountain?

faq.a: No. Straiton Mountain Estates (4595 Sumas Mountain Road, EPS1299) is a bare-land strata of detached houses: you own a strata lot and the house on it, pay strata fees, follow the bylaws, and get a Form B — there is no shared building envelope and no rented pad.
faq.q: What is Straiton, then — is it the mountain's mobile park?

faq.a: Gated is not 55+. The registered bylaws on the Form B are the only operative source for any purchase.
faq.q: Is Straiton 55+?

faq.a: The home only — a chattel. You rent the pad under the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act; the sale takes effect only when registered in the Manufactured Home Registry (Bill of Sale + Notice to Transfer via a lawyer or notary, CSA label attached); and the existing pad tenancy is assigned to you on the same terms, with the park owner's written consent requested on RTB Form 10 — answered by the 10th day or deemed given, no consent fee.
faq.q: If I buy on a rented pad elsewhere in Abbotsford, what do I own?

faq.a: You would own a strata lot, pay strata fees and get a Form B, but there is no shared building and no half-duplex unit.
faq.q: Is Straiton a duplex or townhouse complex?

faq.a: Yes. City zoning (Bylaw 2400-2014) and Abbotsforward 2050 apply on the City side; the FVRD Sumas Mountain OCP (Bylaw No. 584) covers the rural part, which has no public water or sewer — well and septic checks, and rural tax collection by the Province, replace the City items.
faq.q: City side or FVRD side — does it change my diligence?

faq.a: Geotechnical review on slope lots (slopes over 40% and unstable areas sit in the McKee plan's protected open space network), and quarry truck traffic — five quarries operate on the mountain and their gravel trucks use an access road to Highway 1 through the Lightning Rock site.
faq.q: What slope or traffic items surprise buyers here?

faq.a: Two plans apply: the City of Abbotsford Official Community Plan and McKee Neighbourhood Plan on the City side, and the FVRD Sumas Mountain Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 584, for the rural FVRD part.
faq.q: Who plans land use on Sumas Mountain?

faq.a: Yes — a City council report covers gravel extraction at Jamieson Quarry, and Semá:th First Nation states five quarries on Sumas Mountain use an access road to Highway 1.
faq.q: Are there working quarries on Sumas Mountain?
